Slide 4 · Part 1 — Technical Progress

Classification of the Remaining Requirements

The remaining requirements will be organized into the following categories

1

Functional requirements

  • Identify the main functions the system must provide.
  • Define how users will interact with the system.
  • Identify the expected inputs, processing activities, and outputs.
2

Non-functional requirements

  • Performance and reliability.
  • Security and privacy, where applicable.
  • Usability and maintainability.
3

Technical requirements

  • Development environment and software dependencies.
  • Required frameworks, packages, and supporting tools.
  • System architecture and component integration.
4

Testing and evaluation requirements

  • Define how individual components will be tested.
  • Establish criteria for evaluating whether the system meets its requirements.
04 / 10

The next technical step is to classify and document the system requirements properly.\n\nI will separate what the system must do from the technical and quality requirements that determine how well it should operate. I will also identify the testing methods needed to evaluate the implementation.\n\nThis classification will help me organize the development work into manageable tasks rather than beginning implementation without a clear plan.\n\nThese categories represent the requirements-analysis work to be completed and refined; they should not be interpreted as a finalized requirements document.
